title: He's really just a brat
text: By the way, it seems my Father used to train with Tiger Girl to stay in shape. And later on, he was even training by swimming in the ocean with Big Sister’s older sister… Her combat skills are incredible, after all. She’s the kind of person who trains by swimming in the ocean, you know. It must have been a form of training that kept her muscles constantly engaged—far better than lifting some flimsy barbells. The scene from last time, where my Father, dressed as Peckul, was happily swimming in the ocean with my Big Sister’s older sister, was magical and adorable. And if that helps boost their stamina too, it’s killing two birds with one stone.
“I just don’t get why Wolf and Shion are coming up in this conversation. What does Rafumi-chan know?”
“I don’t know anything! It’s not like we’re talking about the future or anything.”
Just what is Rafumi seeing, I wonder!
“Father, whatever the case, Rafumi is teaching Filo-tan some weird stuff!”
Filo-tan would never say something like “loser”! The only ones who’d say something like that are pigs like Griffin, who hang around with Takt!
“Filolial-sama don’t say ‘loser’—they say things like, ‘You’re weak, aren’t you?’, ‘You’re weak, but are you okay?’, or ‘You’ll get beaten somewhere, so you’d better try harder!’”
The Filolial-sama are all compassionate beings—they’re angels who gently offer advice when they see someone is weak.
“I wonder about that, though…”
“It’s still provoking her, though.”
“That’s not true at all!”
And so, for a while, I discussed with my Father the precautions we needed to take regarding the Filolial-sama and Rafumi.
“In any case, we might need to give her a moderate amount of thrills and a sense of danger…”
“Zzz…”
Filo-tan is taking a nap. What an adorable sight. Come to think of it, Filo-tan and Sakura-chan had a lot in common. She’s been laid-back from the very beginning.
“…Well, I guess Filo had this side to her too. Actually, setting Yuki aside, I can’t help but think Kou is almost too good a kid.”
“Is this going to be the part where the conversation shifts to Kou too?　I think he’s a good kid who’s worried about Itsuki and keeps an eye out for anything that might happen…”

“But he’s actually a little brat, you know? I’ve heard he relentlessly targeted Keel’s tail, and did the same to the Bow Hero’s hair, making it all messy. On top of that, he apparently thought he’d eventually eat Imiya and the rest of the Rumo clan.”
“It’s hard to believe that’s the same Kou we know now… I wonder if this was why Motoyasu-kun was so strangely wary of him.”

When he gets lectured by his Father, Kou gets incredibly depressed and turns into a total coward. The cure is for him to spend time with Elephant—that helps him understand what he’s doing wrong and brings back his cheerful self.
“It’s all thanks to Elephant, Elephant.”
“I understand why Motoyasu-kun trusts Elmelo-san so deeply… but by the way, just how important is Elmelo-san to Motoyasu-kun, anyway?”

I’ll think about Father’s question. Well… during a loop, if I were to run into him somewhere, he’d be high enough on my priority list that I’d try to recruit him if I could. There’s a world of difference in the education of the Filolial-sama depending on whether he’s there or not. While free-spirited and carefree Filolial-sama are nice, there’s a line that shouldn’t be crossed—if they cross it, my father-in-law or others might end up lecturing them. If they get too out of hand, they might end up like Kou, and there’s also the risk that Black Thunder could become a completely different person after Rafumi’s attack. When you think about it that way, Zou is a huge help, Zou.
“After Filo-tan, Father, Fitoria-tan, and Filolial-sama, right?”

I suppose that’s about where we should settle on the priority list. Sure, the Big Sisters are important, but first and foremost are the Filolial-sama, starting with Filo-tan. Wouldn’t Elephant be next on the list? Personally, if I had to choose between Elephant and Panda, I’d prioritize Elephant without hesitation. He’s very understanding, after all. Panda didn’t even follow me when I called out to him.
“So, in the end, it’s just that it’s pretty hard to keep Filo-chan the way Motoyasu-kun knows her, huh?”

“It’s the Shield Hero’s fault for spoiling her. You’ve got to let her assert herself a bit more… If you don’t want to, just ignore Filo sometimes—say something like, ‘Oh, Filo… I’d forgotten about you,’ and skip her turn. Act as if you’re naturally swamped taking care of the other slaves.”
“I kind of think that might be abuse, though…”
“The problem is that you’re taking care of her to the point where she thinks she’s satisfied. Desires are, by nature, bottomless, you know?”

My father is absolutely perfect at handling that sort of communication—even with the slaves. In the case of the father who couldn’t save anyone, he tends to be a bit lax about this and just does whatever he wants, but I get the feeling that the father in this loop has become exceptionally skilled in this area. After all, there’s always someone around him. In fact, he’s so dedicated to taking care of others—even cutting into his own sleep time—that the slaves end up keeping watch when it’s time for him to go to bed. Oops, the Father from the first world was the same; Big Sister used to have to remind him to get some sleep. I suppose it’s because he’s taking care of more people than he can realistically handle.
“With Filo-chan, after she gives her report for the day and we play for a bit, if I feed her right after that, she ends up taking a nap.”

“That’s where she’s already starting to turn into a ‘Sakura.’ You should just keep working at a moderate pace while giving her occasional acknowledgments. If she acts spoiled, don’t gently reason with her—just cut her off!”
“Hmm… I get what Rafumi-chan’s trying to do, though.”

“Hmm… It’s quite difficult to strike the right balance. This is a problem where I’ll have to figure out the know-how myself. Well… I do have a plan in place to prevent her from turning into a ‘Sakura,’ though.”
“I don’t know…”
“Spear Hero, I won’t accept any protests, okay? If things keep going like this, you’ll eventually end up tilting your head and asking, ‘Filo…-tan?’ too.”
“Grr…”
Rafumi’s going on about how she’ll stop being “Filo-tan,” but Filo-tan is Filo-tan, after all! So, while I did warn Rafumi about this, I wasn’t able to get her to stop completely.
“Zzz…”

Ah… Filo, tan? Her sleeping face is so adorable today, too. Though, it’s certainly true that she does have an aura similar to Sakura-chan’s. It was the kind of sleeping face that made me feel as though Sakura-chan and Filo-tan were one and the same.
“It’s the circus!”
“It’s the carnival!”
“It’s the caravan!”
Today, just like every other day, the circus caravan is making its rounds through Melromarc.
“The people of Filolial-sama always seem so cheerful—they pull the carriages along happily, shouting with joy every time.”
It’s a fun, fun carriage ride for the people of Filolial-sama. And so, as they tour a new town, the circus tent is erected, and today’s performance begins.
“Oink!”
“Ugh!”
“Ughaaaa!?”

In the opening whipping show performed by the Lazy Pig, the Crocodile Man and Rabbit Man get whipped—and recently, Wolf has also been incorporated into the whipping show. There was a time when they stopped doing it, but due to requests from those who’d heard about it through the grapevine, they had no choice but to bring the act back. However, lately… the opening show hasn’t been going over well with the audience—the applause has been lackluster—and Father was frowning backstage.
“Oink… oink-oink!”
It seems even the Lazy Pig sighs out of sight of the audience right after delivering the lashes.
“Father, does something seem to be wrong?”
Itsuki, who doesn’t participate in the circus, is using her father’s shoulders as a platform to watch the act while perched on his shoulders.
